indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to disgust is to repel

explanation.surface: Revulsion grows towards someone shunned by society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns REPEL upwards, giving LEPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A leper was historically shunned and banished, so the word stands for any social pariah.

clue.text: Off balance when you're out of it!

definitions.text: Off balance when you're out of it!

parts.words: Off balance when you're out of it!
parts.note: the idiom 'out of ...' meaning off balance or not working properly; the thing you are out of is the answer

explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark flags the playful definition: the answer is what you are out of when things are off balance.
explanation.definitionFit: Kilter means good order or balance, and the phrase 'out of kilter' means askew.

indicators.note: one word holding another contains it within its own letters

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
a sign is an indication or piece of evidence

explanation.surface: An informer, keeping hold of proof, finally gave himself up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' reads as an informer (British slang), but here it is the plant; 'holding' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Having resigned something means having given it up or yielded it.

indicators.note: In at the front tells the solver the answer lies inside the following words

explanation.surface: During a match, the players carried off the cup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' signals that the answer runs through gaME MEN TOok.
explanation.definitionFit: A memento is a keepsake, and a trophy is kept as a souvenir of success.

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here the start of Party

parts.note: to object to something is to resent it

explanation.surface: The head of a political party takes exception to gifts of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party leader' looks like a politician, but it gives only P.
explanation.definitionFit: Presents are gifts, and donations are gifts made to a cause.

definitions.note: PM is the abbreviation for post meridiem, the hours after noon; the 's stands for 'is'

indicators.note: deranged means disordered, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister's tirade comes from someone unhinged.
explanation.walkthrough: PM looks like the Prime Minister, but it is post meridiem; 'deranged' rearranges RANT OF ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: PM marks times between midday and midnight, the later part of the day.

indicators.note: one word placed around others encloses them

parts.note: a peter is old criminal slang for a safe
a rim is a border or edge

explanation.surface: A strongbox is placed around the edge of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'safe' looks like an adjective but is criminal slang (as in 'peterman', a safecracker); 'around' is the container signal, and 'English border' gives its pieces border-first.
explanation.definitionFit: A perimeter is the outer boundary of an area, its frontier.

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a raft is a floating platform

explanation.surface: The Labour Party's leader of government needs a policy programme.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour and platform suggest politics (Labour is a British party); here labour is hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: Graft is informal British for hard work, which is what labour means.

indicators.note: heard means the word is spoken, so we want something that sounds the same

parts.note: to take off is to run away, to flee

explanation.surface: A bug is said to run away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' gives the sound of FLEE, spelt as the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A flea is a small jumping parasitic insect.

definitions.meaning: to sit astride something, or to dominate it
to climb on a horse or bicycle with legs either side

explanation.definitionFit: To bestride is to sit or stand with legs either side, as on a horse, and so also to tower over.

indicators.note: is heard means the word is spoken aloud and a soundalike is wanted

parts.note: a lesson can be a moral lecture, a sermon

explanation.surface: A temperate address from the pulpit is listened to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moderate' looks like an adjective describing the sermon, but it is a verb; 'is heard' gives the sound of LESSON.
explanation.definitionFit: To lessen is to reduce or tone down, which is to moderate as a verb.

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here the start of Islamic

parts.note: to run a country is to govern it

explanation.surface: A Muslim ruler presided over a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Islamic leader' suggests an ayatollah, but it gives only I.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is a nation in western Asia.

clue.text: Showering after end of difficult exercise

indicators.note: after puts the word for showering behind the letter
the end of a word is its last letter, here the final letter of difficult

parts.note: when it is showering it is raining

explanation.surface: A tough workout followed by a shower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Showering' suggests washing after the gym, but it is the weather, RAINING.
explanation.definitionFit: Training is a regime of physical exercise.

clue.text: Good man to have in difficulty?

definitions.text: Good man to have in difficulty?

parts.words: Good man to have in difficulty?
parts.note: difficulty read as legal trouble: the professional you want on your side in court

explanation.walkthrough: A barrister is the courtroom advocate in the British legal system.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrister is a British lawyer who argues cases in court, helpful when you are in legal trouble.

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

parts.note: a case is a matter tried in court
a cad is a dishonourable man, a rotter

explanation.surface: A scoundrel takes the blame when his case comes to court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falls' reads as a verb (the villain falls), but it is the noun, a waterfall.
explanation.definitionFit: A cascade is a waterfall, or a series of small falls.

clue.text: Criminal fringe meets resistance from judge

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal
a side is an edge or fringe
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A villain on the margins of society faces opposition from the bench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'judge' looks like the man on the bench but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To consider something is to weigh it up and form an opinion on it.

indicators.note: one word retaining another keeps it inside

parts.note: to expire is to die, to pass on
one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's is a possessive

explanation.surface: Someone dying still clings on to their soul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' gives I, the Roman one.
explanation.definitionFit: Passion is intense feeling or enthusiasm, the fire or spirit someone shows.

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative, the British party
a curate is a junior member of the clergy, a minister of religion

explanation.surface: A Tory government minister is in the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minister' and 'right' suggest politics, but the minister is a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate means correct or exact, just as right does.

indicators.note: a composition puts things together in a new arrangement, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Musical notes pulled taut in a piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' suggests music, matching notes, but signals reordering NOTES IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Straining is the act of stretching tight, which describes tension.

indicators.note: possibly signals that these letters could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A rent reduction might be cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'cut' is a trap: the first is anagram fodder, the second the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To truncate is to shorten by chopping off the end.

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: a camp is a faction or side, a party

explanation.surface: Showy and theatrical behaviour minus a top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'camp' reads as flamboyant, matching 'Pretentious', but it is a faction, PARTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Arty describes something with affected artistic pretensions.

definitions.meaning: to bank is to tilt, as an aircraft does; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.definitionFit: Cant is a slope or tilt, and also sanctimonious, insincere talk.

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: Risqué material shown in a blue programme on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' here suggests indecent material, matching 'Sexy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nubile describes a young woman considered sexually attractive.

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so the word for den comes after

parts.note: a lair is an animal's den

explanation.surface: A hideout chasing a woman is crooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bent' reads as crooked (British slang for dishonest), but it is a natural talent.
explanation.definitionFit: A bent is a natural inclination or talent, as is a flair.

parts.note: the posterior is the backside, the ass

indicators.note: awkwardly means clumsily arranged, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Back up your bottom and sit uncomfortably.
explanation.walkthrough: 'posterior' is a cheeky surface touch; 'awkwardly' jumbles only 'sit', giving the last three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To assist is to help or back up.

clue.text: Special constable with mob following game

indicators.note: following puts the word for mob after the abbreviation

parts.note: SC is the abbreviation for special constable, a volunteer British police officer
a rabble is a disorderly crowd, a mob

explanation.surface: A volunteer policeman is pursued by a crowd for sport.
explanation.walkthrough: A special constable is a volunteer police officer in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrabble is a board game of building words from letter tiles.

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in the Bible

explanation.surface: The President's wife in Paris causes a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First lady' suggests a president's wife but means Eve, the first woman in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: Fever can mean a state of nervous agitation or excitement.

indicators.note: miserable means wretched or in a bad state, so these letters are in disarray

explanation.surface: Holding on to an unhappy longing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'miserable' rearranges CLINGS TO A.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostalgic means wistfully longing for the past.
